game_dll: unchanged: imports the installed ssbu_game_r1.dll; no game rebuild
changes: Upstream 169b467: learned-page snapshot state, late-base desync fix, cheaper rollback ticks, lobby rollback matchmaking
Rollback inputs travel over a direct, token-checked UDP path between the two PCs when one validates (Shared lobby mode); the lobby relay stays as the fallback
Input delay from the measured round trip: covers the one-way trip + 4 ms (2..8 frames; 3 on a ~80-90 ms direct path), rollback only for jitter
The wait for each 60 Hz tick takes the other player's inputs as they arrive instead of after the next frame
This PC's sticks quantized to 8-bit steps with hysteresis before they are sent, so a held stick's noise no longer forces rollbacks
0.5.1: online, port 1 is this PC's player whatever port its controller is on (0.5.0 deadlocked at the match start when the pad was not on port 1)

0.5.2: the handshake gives player i controller slot i, no network flag and the default controls on both PCs (upstream's room-match fix); at most 2 frames past the other player's newest pad (+ SSBU_RB_NET_LATE), then wait; the other game's pads stopped for 8 s = it left: go on

0.5.3: a real pass's capture is skipped when the other player's pad of the next frame is already here (no rollback can load it; about 2 of 3 frames); the last re-run pass after a rollback runs fully (the lite one skipped lighting/camera/effects the next frame shows: fighters in wrong colours)
0.6.0: GameCube adapters in PC mode (Mayflash 0079:1843/1844/1846): an empty port no longer takes a player slot; a controller gets its slot when it first presses a button
0.6.0: online, GameCube controllers are presented as Pro Controllers on both PCs (one controller type for both games)
0.6.0: the lobby build id carries the CoastLink version; the game logs VERSION MISMATCH when someone with the same lobby code runs another version
0.6.0: SSBU_RB_NET_DELAY_PLUS (the app's '1 frame higher' input delay)
0.6.0: graphics.ini audio_device (a waveOut output by name) and mute_background; volume and mute_background apply while the game runs

0.6.2: GameCube adapters in PC mode are read through Windows' own controller support with SDL's GameCube layout (SDL's adapter driver dropped every report that was not 9 or 10 bytes long: with some Mayflash firmware no input arrived); a port SDL has no layout for gets the same one; controllers.ini gamecube_pc = sdl keeps the old way

0.6.2: the WinUSB adapter (Wii U mode) is also found through DeviceInterfaceGUID and through the USB device interface; the log names the driver it found and says when WinUSB was installed on the PC-mode device instead
tested: Controller self-test 68/68 (exercise.py pad), including a PC-mode adapter port without an SDL mapping. Not tested on a physical Mayflash adapter.
